batchSummary: Reviewed all 38 supplied images individually. The draft proposes a coherent Duroflex world built through warm architectural surfaces, directional daylight, tactile detail, supported leisure and restrained brand red. Its strongest spatial references are repeated extensively, while red styling, category-lighting distinctions and room-archetype coverage remain inconsistent. All rules, examples and approval language remain draft proposals—not evidence of adoption, product efficacy or quality approval.

observations.visibleEvidence: An ivory cover pairs large black serif text and small red identifiers with a frontal green-sofa image.
observations.spatialReading: The sofa dominates a concrete-looking room with an orange perforated screen, roof opening, side glazing, dense greenery and a woven-looking rug. Overhead daylight models the cushions and grounds the base.
observations.brandMeaning: Soft upholstery contrasts with substantial architecture, proposing calm without an empty setting.
observations.application: Borrow daylight, framed greenery and clear product hierarchy; adapt architectural hardness and colours around the exact sofa.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The cover explicitly identifies a draft blueprint; product and material authenticity are unverified.

observations.visibleEvidence: A white serif-led page contains an identity-system inset and a dark motion-sofa banner. The inset shows a red symbol/uppercase wordmark, sans-serif messaging and rounded layered panels.
observations.spatialReading: The banner places an olive seat against wine-coloured surroundings. A person in a dark top and pale trousers reclines with legs supported; tables and a tall vase occupy the right.
observations.brandMeaning: The stated shift is from identity components toward a fuller visual world.
observations.application: Retain supported use and product prominence; distinguish graphic panels from room treatments.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The page asserts an evolution; it does not independently establish adoption or chronology.

observations.visibleEvidence: Four image groups accompany a five-language diagnosis: small promotional cards, a wine/olive sofa banner, a daylight mattress room and a dark neck-device portrait.
observations.spatialReading: The mattress sits centrally within a beam-and-screen room; two people interact on its surface. The device portrait removes architecture, while the sofa banner uses a stage-like backdrop.
observations.brandMeaning: Lighting, environment and graphic intensity visibly vary by category.
observations.application: Unify spatial and lighting principles without erasing category-specific product colours.
observations.authorityAndLimits: This is the draft author's diagnosis, not a complete current-channel audit.

observations.visibleEvidence: White serif statements occupy a black page beside a white-bordered image of a seated person using a dark foot device.
observations.spatialReading: A cream outfit and white sofa contrast with blue walls. An arch, stairs, rear window and several lamps establish a domestic setting; the device rests on the rug beneath the person's feet.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition connects everyday stillness with a broader restoration narrative.
observations.application: Borrow credible seated contact and domestic context for recovery-category imagery; simplify competing lamps and décor.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Neither the pose nor the written arc demonstrates stress relief or renewed energy.

observations.visibleEvidence: An eight-part contents list sits beside a red messaging panel and a forest sale banner with white display lettering and a red lower strip.
observations.spatialReading: No interior is shown. A person in flowing yellow clothing reclines on a reddish chair among rocks, water and exposed roots; a dog occupies the foreground.
observations.brandMeaning: The examples span core messaging and expressive promotional activation.
observations.application: Borrow clear campaign hierarchy, not the elaborate outdoor staging as an everyday-room template.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The embedded offer is campaign-specific. Scene authenticity, terrain support and practical motion clearance are unverified.

observations.visibleEvidence: A black section divider frames an exposed blue mattress with visible Duroflex and airboost markings.
observations.spatialReading: A frontal view centres the grey bed within a dark beam grid, translucent screens and an open garden edge. One person sits in a grey top and red shorts; another lies prone in pale clothing, supported on the mattress.
observations.brandMeaning: Product visibility and informal interaction connect the proposition to ordinary companionship.
observations.application: Borrow mattress legibility and supported contact; adapt the strongly themed architecture rather than copying it.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The reference does not verify SKU construction; red clothing also conflicts with later draft restrictions.

observations.visibleEvidence: A red lowercase serif Duroflex rendering, tiny tagline and large serif section title accompany rounded image tiles showing blue and mustard sofas, a mattress, recliner and surface detail.
observations.spatialReading: Neutral walls, daylight and greenery recur, while a seaside arch introduces a more theatrical setting. Products remain dominant within individual tiles.
observations.brandMeaning: The montage proposes category breadth within a shared warm environment.
observations.application: Borrow the consistent neutral support around differing product colours; simplify destination-like scenery.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The rendered wordmark and inset product labels are not validated identity or SKU masters.

observations.visibleEvidence: The black/red headline states a shift from mattress to restoration. Five panels combine a bedroom, product-world boards and human-use examples.
observations.spatialReading: The largest room has a low dark platform bed, cream bedding, olive throw and tall left opening with sheer curtains. Side light reveals wall texture and keeps a clear foreground.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition broadens Duroflex from a product category toward lived experience.
observations.application: Borrow openness and quiet layering, but expose the exact mattress when product explanation is the objective.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The dressed bed illustrates atmosphere, not identifiable mattress performance.

observations.visibleEvidence: People stretch, recline, read and lie with eyes closed above three room references. The title highlights 'Energy' in red.
observations.spatialReading: Pillows support heads and upper bodies. Below, a sunlit cream lounge, lamp-lit bedside corner and pale bedroom with red runner and ottoman show different rest settings.
observations.brandMeaning: The stated stress-to-energy arc is illustrated mainly through stillness and relaxed activity.
observations.application: Borrow supported poses and restrained domestic activity; avoid staging a dramatic before/after transformation.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The collage does not establish emotional states, a chronological recovery sequence or health outcomes.

observations.visibleEvidence: A large black/red serif title faces five small red subheads with black bullet points on an ivory field.
observations.spatialReading: No room or person is shown; the right-hand list occupies only a narrow portion of the page.
observations.brandMeaning: The text proposes visible cues for stress relief, restoration, trust, energy and innovation.
observations.application: Translate these into observable shot choices rather than benefit claims.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The page supplies propositions, not depicted product-quality or scientific evidence.

observations.visibleEvidence: The red word 'quieter' anchors a serif headline beside repeated product, people and room boards plus a larger bedside crop.
observations.spatialReading: The crop layers a bed edge, timber-looking cabinet, warm lamp, branch-filled vessel and foreground water carafe. Tight framing communicates proximity rather than architectural openness.
observations.brandMeaning: Quietness is expressed through low-contrast surfaces and modest domestic actions.
observations.application: Borrow tactile intimacy for supporting details; reduce accessories when the product must lead.
observations.authorityAndLimits: This is a visual metaphor, not evidence of acoustic quietness or restoration efficacy.

observations.visibleEvidence: The philosophy statement accompanies product boards, a cream lounge and a large wall vignette combining vertical slats, an arched niche and rough stone-looking texture.
observations.spatialReading: A floating cabinet and recessed shelves organise ceramics, books and plants. Side light reveals depth; the lounge adds a low round table and woven-looking rug.
observations.brandMeaning: Warmth is constructed through tonal relationships and tactile variation.
observations.application: Borrow the restrained colour relationships; adapt by selecting fewer surfaces and ornaments.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The text names a contemporary Indian direction; pixels do not establish geographic origin or material composition.

observations.visibleEvidence: A sparse ivory page uses a black/red serif title and three vertically stacked style lists. GREEN, AMBER and RED headings are all rendered in red.
observations.spatialReading: No room is shown; the categories are textual filters, not visual swatches.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition favours selective borrowing over stylistic imitation.
observations.application: Evaluate reference features individually instead of importing an entire named style.
observations.authorityAndLimits: These are draft preferences, not adopted exclusions or evidence that a particular room belongs to a style.

observations.visibleEvidence: Five red principle headings with small black explanations sit opposite the large 'Approval before assets' title.
observations.spatialReading: No room, product or person is depicted.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposed filter balances calm with warmth, premium presentation with restraint, and human presence with unforced behaviour.
observations.application: Use the principles as review questions before selecting surfaces, poses and layouts.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The word 'Approval' describes a proposed process; this page grants no asset or quality approval.

observations.visibleEvidence: Two bedrooms and two resting-person crops illustrate the proposed logo-independent signature. One room uses red art, cushions, a foreground throw and mattress trim; the other uses olive accents.
observations.spatialReading: Both rooms employ pale walls and large openings. The people rest against pillows, with clothing and bedding visibly draped around supported bodies.
observations.brandMeaning: The draft seeks recognition through environment and body language beyond a logo.
observations.application: Borrow light and soft geometry; resolve excess red styling and preserve only verified SKU trim.
observations.authorityAndLimits: No recognition test or authentic product specification is supplied.

observations.visibleEvidence: A calm product montage is labelled DO; a crowded red bedroom with three smiling, outward-gesturing people is labelled DON'T.
observations.spatialReading: Red walls, bedding, rugs and outfits compete with framed art, lamps and glossy-looking tables. Dense foreground props compress circulation; a bright glare intensifies the display-like scene.
observations.brandMeaning: The contrast rejects simultaneous chromatic, decorative and performative intensity.
observations.application: Borrow the clear comparison method; assess product hierarchy, usable space and supported natural activity separately.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The negative example is exaggerated and does not establish a precise acceptance threshold.

observations.visibleEvidence: A section divider gives most of its image area to a cream-and-olive bedroom.
observations.spatialReading: The three-quarter view shows a low dark platform, upholstered-looking headboard, woven-looking rug and tall left garden opening. Sheers filter daylight; leaf shadows cross the textured wall. The right crop limits assessment of circulation.
observations.brandMeaning: Architecture and light carry the calm more than decorative branding.
observations.application: Borrow genuine wall space and indoor-outdoor depth; widen the frame when full SKU edges and access routes matter.
observations.authorityAndLimits: No person, material specification or verified room scale is provided.

observations.visibleEvidence: Bedroom, wall, lounge and product-board references support the statement 'Warm Indian modernism.'
observations.spatialReading: Large openings, sheers, low furniture and pale textured surfaces recur. The lounge has an open route behind the sofa, while the wall vignette uses a recessed arch and floating cabinet.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition combines contemporary domestic warmth with an indoor-outdoor relationship.
observations.application: Borrow openings and layered neutrals; adapt generous proportions and highly ordered styling to a believable home.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Climate awareness and cultural specificity are stated aims, not verified properties of these references.

observations.visibleEvidence: Two bedroom boards sit above a frontal green-bed image with an exposed grey-sided mattress.
observations.spatialReading: The bed is centred against a tall pale wall, flanked by narrow sea-view openings and compact round bedside units. A timber-looking ceiling and bordered rug frame it; diagonal daylight crosses the wall.
observations.brandMeaning: Symmetry and visible mattress edges prioritise product clarity.
observations.application: Borrow the frontal product read; adapt side clearances, decorative rug and destination-like outlook.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The pictured high green headboard does not directly illustrate every stated cue, including pale wood and low forms.

observations.visibleEvidence: Living-world boards accompany a teal sofa on a taupe backdrop, a mustard footrest close-up with exposed mechanism and a pale upholstery detail against wine.
observations.spatialReading: The lower images are product studies, not rooms. Upper insets show low seating, broad tables and warm interior-to-exterior views.
observations.brandMeaning: Silhouette, surface and visible construction extend the architectural story into product detail.
observations.application: Borrow complementary environment and close-detail coverage; preserve exact seams, upholstery and mechanism geometry.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Social ease is stated but not enacted here; materials and mechanical operation remain unverified.

observations.visibleEvidence: Five references accompany four named archetypes: bedroom, lounge, seaside-arch recliner, wall niche and lamp-lit bedside corner.
observations.spatialReading: The bedroom and lounge receive strong side daylight. The recliner sits beneath a flower-framed arch; the bedside crop feels enclosed and intimate.
observations.brandMeaning: The menu proposes different settings for reset, release, recovery and retail.
observations.application: Borrow category-appropriate openness or intimacy; simplify theatrical scenery and clarify which image demonstrates each archetype.
observations.authorityAndLimits: No identifiable retail zone is shown. The recliner image's darkened lower edge is not permission to add photographic fades.

observations.visibleEvidence: A quiet-wall proposition is illustrated through a slatted niche wall, bedside corner, mattress board, restrained red-accent bedroom and crowded red display.
observations.spatialReading: Broad pale wall areas support the beds, while the niche combines several textures and shelf objects. The crowded display interrupts surfaces with art, lamps and props.
observations.brandMeaning: The intended distinction is background support versus visual competition.
observations.application: Borrow low-contrast wall depth; simplify the multi-surface vignette rather than reproducing every layer.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The mixed collage requires interpretation; not every included image is explicitly labelled positive or negative.

observations.visibleEvidence: The heading says 'Approved surfaces' beside a niche wall, sunlit bedroom, room boards and warm bedside crop.
observations.spatialReading: Slat rhythm, mottled wall appearance, rough stone-looking relief and soft curtains supply different scales of texture. Side light makes these visible without strong colour contrast.
observations.brandMeaning: The draft favours tactile interest over graphic wall pattern.
observations.application: Borrow one dominant wall treatment with quieter supporting surfaces; adapt texture density to the exact product.
observations.authorityAndLimits: 'Approved' remains draft language. The listed limewash, travertine and other materials cannot be confirmed from these images.

observations.visibleEvidence: The red display room appears twice beside contact sheets of identity, product and promotional assets.
observations.spatialReading: Dense furniture, décor and saturated surfaces dominate the room; presenter-like gestures add activity. The contact sheets are graphic archives, not additional architectural examples.
observations.brandMeaning: The stated rejection targets visual overload and showroom-like competition.
observations.application: Avoid cumulative clutter; do not treat every historical asset visible in the contact sheets as rejected.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Several listed exclusions, such as neon panels, are not clearly demonstrated. Small thumbnails do not support detailed asset judgements.

observations.visibleEvidence: Bedroom, lounge and bedside references repeatedly show large woven-looking rugs, pale flooring and warm brown furniture; a brighter bedroom shows wood-looking floorboards.
observations.spatialReading: Rugs define furniture zones and soften the foreground. Side lighting reveals pile or weave while shadows beneath beds and tables establish contact.
observations.brandMeaning: Grounding comes from layered surfaces rather than reflective spectacle.
observations.application: Borrow quiet floor continuity and coherent base shadows; keep rug edges and access routes plausible.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The named wood species and floor finishes are proposals, not visually verified specifications.

observations.visibleEvidence: The 'Skin-trust palette' page combines rumpled cream bedding, a textured chair, water carafe, mustard footrest detail and two bed scenes.
observations.spatialReading: The bedside crop is tightly layered around a low round table and warm lamp. Wider bed references use neutral walls with green or red accents.
observations.brandMeaning: Texture and approachable domestic objects suggest sensory warmth.
observations.application: Borrow readable weave, drape and cushion modelling without modifying the SKU's actual surface.
observations.authorityAndLimits: No skin contact is shown here; the images establish neither skin safety, fabric composition nor comfort performance.

observations.visibleEvidence: People wear loose cream, sage and muted-rose clothing while sitting, reading, holding a mug or leaning together. A second panel shows textured bedding and a lamp-lit corner.
observations.spatialReading: Bent legs, cushions and floor seating create close body-to-surface relationships. Hanging garments repeat the muted palette; foreground furniture makes the room crop intimate.
observations.brandMeaning: Unforced activity links tactile surroundings to everyday living.
observations.application: Borrow relaxed styling and small actions; verify weight-bearing contact and keep wardrobe secondary to the product.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The listed fibres and 'breathability' are not demonstrated material properties.

observations.visibleEvidence: A slatted niche wall, low round lounge table, bedside cabinet and product-world boards illustrate 'Warm craft.'
observations.spatialReading: Grain-like markings and uneven pale surfaces contrast with soft upholstery. Left-side daylight grazes relief, while the lamp-lit crop adds amber warmth and closer object layering.
observations.brandMeaning: Hard surfaces are positioned as tactile partners to softness, not cold technical scenery.
observations.application: Borrow restrained surface contrast; reduce heavy stone-looking masses and shelf décor if they overpower the SKU.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Stone type, wood species, terracotta and brushed-metal composition are not established by these references.

observations.visibleEvidence: The nature page repeats a garden-opening bedroom, planted niche, cream lounge and category boards.
observations.spatialReading: The bedroom connects interior and exterior through tall glazing, sheers and leaf shadows. Other examples rely more on potted plants, including trailing greenery in a recess and plants beside seating.
observations.brandMeaning: Nature is proposed as part of spatial experience rather than a decorative badge.
observations.application: Borrow framed views and source-consistent shadows; adapt plant placement into one coherent architectural zone.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Courtyards and structural planters are stated options, but the visible evidence chiefly shows openings and pots.

observations.visibleEvidence: The instruction 'Fewer, better plants' accompanies rooms containing both substantial greenery and several smaller potted accents.
observations.spatialReading: The lounge has a large plant near the window, trailing niche greenery and tabletop planting. The bedside corner layers a tall branch-filled vessel with smaller plants around furniture.
observations.brandMeaning: The intended hierarchy is one strong natural presence, though the examples are less selective.
observations.application: Consolidate greenery and remove redundant small pots; retain clear circulation and the product silhouette.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The imagery does not consistently demonstrate the stated reduction in scattered decoration.

observations.visibleEvidence: Sunlit bedroom and lounge references accompany the proposal to own soft restorative light; product boards and a brighter red-trim bedroom complete the page.
observations.spatialReading: Visible left openings motivate illumination. Leaf patterns, diagonal floor shadows and warm highlights reveal surfaces, although some sun edges are comparatively defined.
observations.brandMeaning: Recognisability is proposed through a lighting character rather than room colour alone.
observations.application: Borrow motivated daylight and gentle modelling; maintain exact product colour and coherent shadows without haze or blur treatments.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Time of day and restorative effects cannot be established from the pictures.

observations.visibleEvidence: A bedroom board with exposed blue-sided mattresses sits above two dressed beds: one cream/olive, one pale with red accents.
observations.spatialReading: Tall openings, light bedding and readable bed edges support a fresh atmosphere. The olive room shows warm leaf shadows; the red-accent room is more evenly bright.
observations.brandMeaning: The text proposes a morning mood for sleep products.
observations.application: Borrow daylight clarity and open framing; adapt surrounding colours to the actual mattress rather than recolouring it blue-white.
observations.authorityAndLimits: 'Morning' and 'breathable' describe intended presentation, not verified timing or airflow.

observations.visibleEvidence: A large frontal green-bed scene is combined with bedroom boards, a warm bedside corner, pale upholstery against wine and a red-accent bedroom.
observations.spatialReading: The green bed has clear mattress edges, compact side tables and narrow sea-view openings. Direct daylight crosses its pale wall; the other panels introduce warmer or more saturated lighting contexts.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition prioritises calm product legibility for explanatory channels.
observations.application: Borrow clear silhouette and neutral exposure; standardise colour handling for catalogue use.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The collage is not a consistent neutral-light specification or a current website sample.

observations.visibleEvidence: An evening-mood statement accompanies a teal sofa on taupe, mustard mechanism detail, seaside-arch recliner, sunlit lounge and living-world board.
observations.spatialReading: Soft studio modelling isolates the sofa, while the architectural references include bright exterior sky and substantial daylight rather than uniformly low evening light.
observations.brandMeaning: Tactile richness is more consistently demonstrated than the stated wine/olive/walnut evening palette.
observations.application: Borrow warm environmental support and detail coverage; preserve teal, mustard or other exact SKU colours.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The examples do not establish a single approved evening treatment.

observations.visibleEvidence: Neutral bedrooms with red art, cushions, runners, trim and an ottoman are contrasted with the crowded red display and category boards.
observations.spatialReading: Pale walls and daylight keep the quieter rooms legible, but repeated red objects create several competing accents. The crowded room distributes red across almost every layer.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposition separates brand recognition from an entirely red environment.
observations.application: Borrow restrained graphic identification; resolve which environmental accents are permitted and preserve only verified product details.
observations.authorityAndLimits: These examples conflict with the later draft prohibition on red bedding and props.

observations.visibleEvidence: A written palette accompanies cream/olive rooms, blue and mustard sofas, muted clothing and product-world boards. Red remains prominent in the page's wordmark and headline.
observations.spatialReading: Pale architectural fields provide continuity; darker upholstery and olive textiles create depth. Daylit openings and warm brown furniture connect the bedroom and lounge.
observations.brandMeaning: The proposed world is neutral-led but not colourless.
observations.application: Let the exact SKU anchor colour relationships; choose complementary room and wardrobe layers rather than forcing every listed hue.
observations.authorityAndLimits: This is a descriptive draft palette, not measured swatches or an exhaustive product-colour rule.

observations.visibleEvidence: The category-accent statement is illustrated by a large teal sofa, mustard footrest detail, beige recliner beneath an arch and a warm bedside corner.
observations.spatialReading: The imagery alternates between isolated product study, theatrical exterior outlook and close domestic detail. No complete recovery-device setting is visible.
observations.brandMeaning: The text proposes category variation without a change of identity.
observations.application: Borrow neutral support and tactile continuity; adapt light and room context rather than enforcing category colours on products.
observations.authorityAndLimits: Blue-white sleep and spa-tech recovery are not clearly demonstrated by this selection.

observations.visibleEvidence: Two dense product-world boards and a portrait bedroom reference accompany a proposed 25–40% breathing-space target.
observations.spatialReading: The bedroom contains genuine pale wall and floor area, but the bed fills much of its width and a red ottoman competes near the foreground. Large slide margins are outside the photograph.
observations.brandMeaning: The intended hierarchy is one important product within a calm setting.
observations.application: Create space through camera position and architecture—not white patches, masks or fades.
observations.authorityAndLimits: The percentage is a draft proposal; these examples do not demonstrate a measured photographic ratio.

relationships.finding: The proposed spatial language is clearest in the repeatedly used cream-and-olive bedroom.
relationships.interpretation: A low horizontal bed, tall left opening, sheer curtain, textured wall, woven-looking rug and leaf shadows work together. Borrow this relationship between architecture and light, not the reference bed or its exact décor.

relationships.finding: The draft's restoration narrative broadly aligns with the supplied positioning, but the images illustrate mood rather than efficacy.
relationships.interpretation: Everyday pause, supportive presence and renewed readiness are compatible with 'Motivating Reset.' Neither resting poses nor calm rooms prove stress mitigation, physical recovery or a dramatic transformation.

relationships.finding: Category breadth can coexist with a shared environment without recolouring products.
relationships.interpretation: Blue mattresses, green beds, teal and mustard sofas, and beige recliners retain distinct appearances against predominantly warm, quiet surroundings. The room should adapt to the exact SKU; category palette descriptions should not override it.

relationships.finding: Supported contact is more useful than generic smiling as a human-direction cue.
relationships.interpretation: Visible examples include legs on an extended footrest, feet placed in a floor device, bodies resting on mattresses and heads supported by pillows. Books, mugs and companionship supply modest lived activity without requiring presenter gestures.

relationships.finding: Red is consistently proposed as identification, but the illustrated environmental boundary is unresolved.
relationships.interpretation: The crowded red room is clearly negative, yet ostensibly calmer examples still use red cushions, throws, runners, art and furniture. The later prohibition on red bedding and props needs reconciliation with these draft examples.

relationships.finding: The nature references demonstrate framed greenery more convincingly than a strict one-plant approach.
relationships.interpretation: Large openings and leaf shadows create an architectural relationship with nature. Several lounge, niche and bedside examples nevertheless scatter smaller pots across shelves and tables; one coherent green zone would express the stated hierarchy more clearly.

relationships.finding: Morning, neutral-day and evening modes are not yet separated reliably by the chosen examples.
relationships.interpretation: The same sunlit lounge and bedroom recur across different purposes, while the evening page includes bright sky and daylight. Distinct lighting references are needed if these modes are to become reproducible production directions.

relationships.finding: Product-detail imagery supplies a useful complement to room atmosphere.
relationships.interpretation: Visible weave, upholstery curvature, fabric drape and exposed motion hardware offer concrete subjects for close shots. They can explain appearance and construction without substantiating fibre identity, breathability, skin safety or mechanical performance.

relationships.finding: Rendered typography and logo treatments are not consistent enough to serve as final identity specifications.
relationships.interpretation: The opening pages use serif deck text; the identity inset shows an uppercase symbol/wordmark and sans-serif messaging; later pages display a lowercase serif Duroflex rendering. Font substitution and draft assembly must be resolved against authoritative artwork.

relationships.finding: The same small reference library carries many different arguments.
relationships.interpretation: Repeated bedrooms, the arched niche, cream lounge and lamp-lit corner establish consistency, but repetition is not independent evidence of broad applicability across homes, products, lighting conditions or channels.

relationships.finding: The four-room menu has uneven visual coverage.
relationships.interpretation: Bedroom and lounge settings are well represented, and V004 offers a domestic device-use example. A clearly planned recovery corner and a credible Retail Calm Zone are not demonstrated; contact sheets and decorative wall vignettes do not fill that gap.

relationships.finding: Photographic breathing space must be distinguished from page-layout whitespace.
relationships.interpretation: Real walls, openings and floor area can support product hierarchy. Ivory slide margins and bordered insets cannot demonstrate the proposed in-scene space ratio, nor justify adding artificial contrast patches or fades.

relationships.finding: Highly themed settings require stronger adaptation than the neutral domestic references.
relationships.interpretation: Forest staging, a strongly gridded-screen room and flower-framed seaside arches are more literal and theatrical than the proposed everyday contemporary home. Borrow openness, filtered light or sheltered seating—not destination-wellness luxury or complete stylistic sets.

contradictions: V006 depicts red shorts, while V009, V015 and V035 include red bedding or props; supplied V128 explicitly lists red outfits, bedding and props as DON'Ts. These draft examples need reconciliation, not automatic approval.
V030 asks for one substantial plant or architectural greenery, but its lounge and bedside examples distribute several smaller plants across niches, tables and furniture.

V034's evening description specifies low warm light and wine/olive/walnut, yet its prominent examples include teal and mustard products, bright exterior sky and a sunlit lounge. Resolve the reference selection without recolouring the products.
V021 names four room archetypes but presents five loosely mapped images, none clearly demonstrating retail circulation, display planning or a Retail Calm Zone.

V013 advises borrowing rather than copying styles, while V006 and V021 use strongly themed architectural settings. This is a tension in literalness, not evidence that a geographic origin can be inferred from the images.
V038 states a photographic breathing-space target, but much of its apparent openness is slide-layout margin. The proposed ratio is not demonstrated within the room images.
gaps: Only V001–V038 were visually reviewed in this batch. Other supplied guide passages are textual context; the remaining pages of the 151-slide draft were not visually assessed here.
Final logo artwork, authoritative typography and adopted graphic specifications are absent. PPTX font substitution may explain some rendered differences.

No verified SKU asset pack establishes exact colour, fabric, branding, dimensions or construction for the reference products. Scene imagery may be synthetic, and material names cannot be authenticated from pixels.
The supplied May 2025 positioning provides strategy, not exact-product efficacy substantiation. No health, airflow, recovery or skin-safety claims can be certified from this batch.
Embedded campaigns and contact sheets do not constitute a dated public-site or social audit. Their offers, product names and graphic treatments are not permanent brand rules.
Distinct production examples are needed for retail, recovery-device settings, ordinary room scales and clearly differentiated morning/day/evening lighting.
Still images cannot verify motion clearance, mechanism operation, complete anatomy or sustained body-product contact. No videos were reviewed.
No measured crop tests, recognition studies, adoption decisions or completed approval records establish that the proposed visual signature or breathing-space rule has been validated.
